9 h 20 min until the 12:00 freeze. Four decisions before I plan; my recommendation is first in each.

> **Question to the user**
> - The crack transition: how should it change the picture? A real split with both looks on screen needs the old look kept somewhere while the new one spreads.
>   - Frozen old frame (Recommended): When a cut lands (the card closes), the last frame of the old look is captured; the new look switches on underneath; a glowing jagged vertical crack opens in the middle and runs to both edges, revealing the new look, ~0.7 s, the fight paused meanwhile. Robust, works for every layer, HUD included.
>   - Live in every material: Each material knows the crack position and draws old or new on its side, both live. Truer, but every material, the HUD and the effects need a split version: far more work and risk before 12:00.
> - Niagara or effects built in code? Niagara graphs can't be authored reliably from headless scripts (the Unreal MCP is down), so every Niagara system would be a guess I can't tune by eye in the editor.
>   - Code-driven particles (Recommended): Our own pooled particle system in C++ (instanced meshes, neon materials): sparks on hits, slash ribbons, dust and embers on the slam, shuriken trails, money bursts, footstep dust. Fully testable and tunable from frames. Credited honestly as not Niagara.
>   - Niagara, best effort: I create Niagara systems from engine templates by script and drive their parameters from C++. Slower, riskier, some may look generic.
> - Three tiers of effects. Today cut 1 removes the hero's effects and cut 2 turns the world grey. Which mapping?
>   - Full / medium / bare (Recommended): Before cut 1: the new rich particles plus today's effects. After cut 1: only today's effects (medium). After cut 2 (grey world): bare greybox effects (flat grey shapes, no glow). Readability warnings for his attacks stay in every tier.
>   - Keep the layer cuts as they are: Rich particles are simply part of the effects layer and all go at cut 1 together; no medium tier.
> - If time runs short before 12:00, what goes first?
>   - Details, crack, then effects (Recommended): 1) katana in hand in every pose, shurikens from the throwing hand, smooth moves and transitions; 2) the crack transition; 3) the rich effects, as many as fit. A packaged build after each, not pushed.
>   - Effects, crack, then details: The look first, the hand-and-katana details last.
>   - Crack, effects, then details: The transition first.

Sunday afternoon: one combined task, run in parallel

The author played session-5n: "everything else is great". This prompt replaces PROMPT_full_tier_look.md and PROMPT_aura_shuriken_locomotion.md (do not run them separately).

How to run it

You are the orchestrator. Split the work into tracks and hand each to a lead agent in its own git worktree, as many leads as you judge right (the tracks below are a suggestion, merge or split them). Each lead works test first in its worktree, then reports to you: what changed, tests, a screenshot or short clip of the look, open questions. You review every report against this prompt, send it back if it falls short, and land approved branches on main one at a time, running the full test suite after each landing.

The author approved the parallel run in advance: post a one-line forecast (number of agents, rough tokens, time) and start without waiting.

Constraints for the leads:





The Unreal editor and the Unreal MCP are shared, and a build closes the editor. Agree slots: only one lead at a time works in the editor or builds. Binary assets (.uasset, Niagara systems, the level) cannot be merged: give each asset to exactly one track.



Balance numbers live in [JamBalance] in Config/DefaultGame.ini; decisions in the pure *Rules with Jam.* tests, red first.



Questions to the author go through you, as interactive questions, batched.



We are past the 12:00 feature stop. Aim to land everything by about 17:00; whatever is not solid by then is left out and goes in the DEVLOG as not done. The final build must be stable: the video is recorded from it at 18:00.

Track A: two quick fixes (land first, small)





The Ultimate charge aura says nothing while the meter fills. Bring back the Ultimate meter as its own bar under the hero's health, in every tier, as before T-072. The red aura under the hero shows only when the meter is full (and through the wind-up), never earlier. Shape ronin and greybox: the bar always, their ready cue only when full.



The hero's shurikens: 30% more per second, the same damage per second. Hero cooldown 0.4 s to about 0.31 s, damage per shuriken 9 to about 6.9 (round as the code allows, DPS within 2%). The hero only: the Publisher's stolen shuriken keeps exactly his current damage, spacing and speed. ShurikenCooldown and ShurikenDamage are shared with his stolen copy (scaled by BossStolenCooldown, BossShurikenCooldownScale, BossStolenDamage), so give him his own base keys or compensate his scales, and pin his current numbers with a test before the change. The hero's explosive shuriken (ShurikenExplosiveEvery=3) would explode 30% more often: ask the author whether to keep explosions per second the same (every 4th) or keep every 3rd.

Track B: the full-art tier must be the most beautiful

The author: the hit effects still look like a lower tier (small flat sparks, red on the hero). The top tier should be as beautiful as we can make it so the fall to the lower tiers is felt. No hardware ray tracing (judges' GPUs may lack it).





Remove the flat greybox layer from the full-art tier. AJamEffectsView::DrawBurst (Source/JamGame/Private/View/JamEffectsView.cpp) still draws plain discs in every tier: hit, slam, explosion, deflect, heal. In the full-art tier Niagara alone shows these events; the discs stay in shape ronin and greybox. Keep anything that carries gameplay information (telegraph circles, the slam warning) unless a Niagara version replaces it clearly. The tier choice is a rule with a test.



Rework the T-069 Niagara systems (/Game/FX/NS_JamHitSparks, NS_JamSlamDust, NS_JamCashBurst, NS_JamTrail, NS_JamEmbers; built on two simple materials, then cut down, the trail never checked by eye): hits get a bright core flash with a short-lived point light, more and longer streaks; slams and blasts a shockwave ring; cash bursts sparkle. Keep the Publisher readable (prefer light and streaks over big opaque sprites, he washed white before). Check every effect by eye from the game camera.



Lighting and post process for the full-art tier only: Lumen GI and reflections, bloom, cyan and magenta neon lights in the arena, emissive surfaces that light the floor, slight vignette and grading. Lower tiers turn them off step by step (shape ronin: flat light, no bloom; greybox: unlit and bare). Read the current settings in Config/DefaultEngine.ini and the level first and report what is on.



Hold 60 fps on a mid-range GPU: log frame times in a busy moment (Ultimate plus slam). If Lumen costs too much, fall back to simpler light rather than dropping the look.

Track C: directional locomotion

The author: wherever the hero moves, his legs run straight forward along his facing; the feet should step where he actually moves (strafing, backpedalling, diagonals). In another project they used Orientation Warping (Animation Warping plugin) in an Animation Blueprint: a forward walk sequence, Local To Component, Orientation Warping fed by the locomotion direction angle, Component To Local, plus a lean blend space driven by yaw delta. It worked there; it is an idea, not a requirement.

Our hero has no Animation Blueprint: UJamPoseInstance blends idle, walk and one action in C++. First a short comparison and a recommendation, sent to the author as interactive questions before code:





Orientation Warping, or the same in C++ (twist pelvis and legs toward the move direction while spine and head keep facing the aim), in our pose instance versus moving to an Animation Blueprint;



directional clips (strafe left and right, backpedal) from the Meshy animation library, their credit cost, blended by a direction angle;



a lean into turns and stride warping (play rate tied to ground speed), which also fixes the Publisher's sliding walk (he moves six times faster than his clip).
The move-direction decision lives in JamPoseRules with tests; the view only applies it. Clip: the hero circling the Publisher and backpedalling. This is the riskiest track: if it is not solid by 17:00, leave it out of the build.

<pasted_content id="27e6">
The author played the main menu (T-092) and the opening comic (T-093): "everything else is very good". The fixes below, then one build. Do not launch the game or take screenshots unless it is the only way to check something: the author validates in play at the end.

Main menu





On a wide or ultrawide screen the backdrop leaves empty strips on both sides, and the dollar sign on top of the Publisher's tower is cut off. Make the city backdrop cover the whole screen at any aspect ratio (scale to cover, or extend its edges with fal outpainting if covering crops too much), and keep the whole tower with its dollar sign in frame.



After their first idle the hero and the Publisher freeze completely. They loop their idle for as long as the menu is open.

Settings





The settings panel is too transparent: the arena shows through and the text is hard to read. Make the panel background much more opaque.



The controls are offset from what is drawn: pressing the arrow next to a value does nothing, only clicking the label (for example "MASTER VOLUME") works. Make the visible arrows and values the real hit areas.



Graphics, window mode and resolution become dropdown lists that open on click (no cycling through every resolution). The three volumes become sliders. Keyboard and mouse both work.

Sound





Voices are too quiet, in the comic and in the fight: raise every voice line by at least 25 to 30%.



The comic plays with the full fight music. Make a new soft neon ambient track with ElevenLabs, in the same key and mood as the main theme (Tools/Audio/eleven_audio.py, add it to the ledger). It plays under the comic and the intro, and crossfades into the full theme when the Publisher finishes his line in the intro, during the kung-fu show-off. If the player skips the intro, the full theme fades in from the moment of the skip.

Comic and steal card





The comic stretches across the whole screen on ultrawide, so attention scatters. Keep the comic at its own aspect ratio, centred, with black bars at the sides, so all of it is always visible.



The steal card ("which move do you lose"): the choices can be clicked with the mouse, not only picked with the key.



The steal card just appears. Give it a short lively entrance: a pop with a slight overshoot and bounce (about 0.3 s, ease-out-back), the two choices following a beat later. A similar light touch on other pop-up panels where it is cheap.

Full-art look





The generated textures look rough up close, most of all on the torii arch in the middle and on the characters. Add a light film look in the full-art tier only: fine film grain, a little rain haze and depth fog, slight chromatic aberration at the edges, and softer detail in the distance, so the texture noise reads as atmosphere. Keep the fighters readable. The lower tiers stay without it.

The end

Tests green (rules for anything decided in code, red first), commit on main, one Shipping package, push to itch, DEVLOG. Report in a few lines: what changed, what you could not check without running the game, the build name and the exe path.

   **Engine findings (UE 5.8 source)**
   - Text blur:
     - AHUD::DrawText makes an FCanvasTextItem with the UFont and sets `TextItem.Scale = (Scale, Scale)`.
     - AHUD::GetTextSize calls `Canvas->TextSize(Font, Text, W, H, Scale, Scale)`.
     - GEngine->MediumFont falls back to `CreateFontObjectFromDefaultFont("DefaultRegularFont","Regular",10)`, a runtime Roboto at LegacyFontSize 10, so text is rasterised at 10 and scaled up: this is the blur.
     - FCanvasTextItem has a ctor `(FVector2D, FText, const FSlateFontInfo&, FLinearColor)`; UFont has `GetLegacySlateFontInfo()`.
   - DPI:
     - `bEnableHighDPIAwareness` defaults to 1, so SetProcessDpiAwareness(PER_MONITOR) runs unless unattended. The game is DPI-aware already; Windows is not stretching it.
     - BaseEngine has `bAllowHighDPIInGameMode=False` (UMG only; we use canvas).

They hide AHUD's, so all 74 call sites in JamHUD*.cpp use them.

**Blur root causes (confirmed in engine source and in logs)**
- `[/Script/Engine.UserInterfaceSettings] bAllowHighDPIInGameMode=False` (engine default) makes the game DPI-unaware. Windows at 125% reports 3440x1440 as 2752x1152 and stretches the picture.
- A first launch has `sg.ResolutionQuality=0`, so `r.ScreenPercentage` stays 0 and the mode falls back to `r.ScreenPercentage.Default.Desktop.Mode=1` (BasedOnDisplayResolution). The `[Rendering.AutoScreenPercentage]` table maps 720→720 and 2160→1080, so a 1152-tall display gets about 72%.
- The menu quality levels map to 50/71/87/100 (`PerfIndexValues_ResolutionQuality`).
- `SetHighDPIMode` is gated in `SlateApplication.cpp` by `bAllowHighDPIInGameMode` for games.

**DLSS (another session, merged into main at f1d0e40)**
- Defaults to QUALITY on RTX at screen percentage 66.7; `-NoDlss` disables it.
- `JamSettings::ApplyDlss` sets `r.ScreenPercentage` after scalability.

Two small fixes to the neon bars from the author's play-through.





The angles do not match: the frame, the plate and the segments slant at slightly different angles, most visible at the right end of the boss bar and on the hero's bars. Cause (the mockup had the same bug): each shape uses the same horizontal slant offset in pixels, but the shapes have different heights (the frame is taller than the segments), so the angle differs. Fix: one shared slope per bar, SlantPerPixel = tan(angle), and every point's x shift is (BottomY - y) * SlantPerPixel, computed from the same bottom line for the frame, the plate, the segments, the cut marks and the name tab. Put it in the Rules function with a test that the frame's and a segment's edges are parallel.



The chunk of recently lost health reads grey. Make it bright white (alpha about 0.9), cut into segments like the fill, fading out as it does now.

Then package and push per Tickets/PROMPT_final_push.md.
</pasted_content id="27e6">

8. Current Work

Implementing the user's slope fix. `JamNeonBarRules::Slanted` and the test `Jam.Hud.NeonFrameAndSegmentsSlantAlike` are written; the implementation was just added after a red run. `JamHUDNeon.cpp` was just read (full content above) and needs converting:

**Slope, one per bar**
- Replace `FNeonPara(X0, Y0, X1, Y1, Slant)` with a constructor from `JamNeonBarRules::Slanted(X0, Y0, X1, Y1, BottomY, Slope)`.
- Use one Slope constant for all bars, about 0.6, e.g. `constexpr float NeonSlope = 0.6f;`, replacing `NeonBossSlant`, `NeonHeroSlant` and `NeonUltimateSlant`.
- `FJamNeonBar::Slant` now means the slope; update the header comment.
- BottomY = the bar's `Box.Max.Y` for the plate, the segments, the glow fill, the chunk, the preview and the cut marks. The boss tab uses the boss bar's BottomY.
- Scanlines: x shift = `(Y1 - y) * Slope`.
- Top edge line: from the segment quad's `Corners[0]` to `Corners[1]`.
- Cut marks: from `(X + (Y1 - (Y0 - Reach)) * Slope, Y0 - Reach)` to `(X + (Y1 - (Y1 + Reach)) * Slope, Y1 + Reach)`.
- Number X: `Box.Max.X + (Y1 - Y0) * Slope + NeonNumberGap`.

**Chunk**
- In the segment loop, for each segment overlapping `[Fill, Chunk]`, draw a quad from `max(From, Fill)` to `min(To, Chunk)` in white at alpha 0.9 × `Bar.Alpha`.
- Change `NeonChunkWhite` to alpha 0.9. Treat the preview the same way.
- Keep the drain behaviour (`JamBarRules::Track`).

Then format (`clang-format`), run `build_and_test.sh`, and commit with a message file.
